Surah: 26. Follow the brief below (surah_map.md) exactly. The evidence is text.md (the surah), dictionary.md (every root of the surah's words, each branch with the classical dictionaries' own phrases), channels.md and hft.md (both are earlier readers' proposals: ignore their judgements (grades, strength or confidence labels, reading types, statements of what a reading may or may not do) and make your own) and your own knowledge of Arabic and the Quran. Return only the map as your final message.

===== _commentary/v16/prompts/r2/surah_map.md =====
Read the surah as one text and write its map of image chains: the lexical images that run through several of
its ayat and join them into one scene, process or movement. A later writer will read one ayah at a time, with
only that ayah's own dictionary. The map lets that writer hear what the ayah's words carry in the surah as a
whole, including senses whose evidence sits under the words of other ayat.

Your evidence is the surah text, the dictionary of every root in the surah (each branch with the classical
dictionaries' own phrases), earlier readers' channel review (channels.md) and activation hypotheses (hft.md),
and your own knowledge of Arabic and the Quran. Where a member or passage comes from memory rather than from
the dictionary or the text, say so. Do not use tools, delegate, browse or inspect files.

The channel review and the HFT records are proposals by earlier readers. Ignore their judgements: grades,
strength or confidence labels, reading types, words such as "surprising", "exploratory" or "latent", and every
statement of what a reading may or may not do. Make your own judgement from the surah's words, the dictionary
phrases and the Quran. Do not rediscover what they already assembled: start from their chains, test each one
against the dictionary phrases and the text, and join, extend, split or correct them. Where their wording
abstracts a member, go back to the dictionary phrase and name what it actually says.

A chain belongs on the map when its members are senses the dictionary attests for words that stand in the
surah, and together they make one image or process that the surah's wording or sequence lets a listener hear.
A member need not be the sense that translates its word in its own ayah; a chain is heard across the surah,
not in one word. Say plainly when a member is a rare sense or is attested only inside a fixed expression, and
keep it. When the dictionary itself joins two of the surah's words in one phrase, quote that phrase: it is
the strongest evidence a chain can have. Keep a scene at the level of its objects, their parts and their
operation. When proposals share members, do not fold one into another's more abstract function unless nothing
concrete is lost. Carry every chain that meets this test, however unusual; leave out proposals that do not.

Write the map in English, with Arabic quoted exactly (surah wording from the text, dictionary phrases from the
dictionary). It is working material for the writer, not commentary prose.

1. `## Chains`. For each chain, a `###` heading naming the image. One paragraph on what the image is and how it
   moves through the surah. Then its members, one line each: the ayah ref, the word as it stands in the text,
   the root and branch id, the dictionary's own phrase quoted exactly, and what this member contributes to the
   image. Add Quran passages outside the surah, with exact refs, where they stage or confirm the chain.
2. `## Ayat`. For each ayah in order: which chains it opens, advances or completes, and what its words add to
   each.
3. `## Not carried`. Each channel subchannel and each HFT record you did not carry into a chain, one line each:
   its name and why.

No ranking and no labels of strength or confidence. No list of what a writer must include. There is no length
target and no required number of chains or members.


===== _commentary/v16/work/s026/surah.r2/text.md =====
# Surah 26

- 26:1 طسٓمٓ
- 26:2 تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
- 26:3 لَعَلَّكَ بَٰخِعٌۭ نَّفْسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُوا۟ مُؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:4 إِن نَّشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ ءَايَةًۭ فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَٰقُهُمْ لَهَا خَٰضِعِينَ
- 26:5 وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا۟ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضِينَ
- 26:6 فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا۟ فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أَنۢبَٰٓؤُا۟ مَا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
- 26:7 أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۢ كَرِيمٍ
- 26:8 إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:9 وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
- 26:10 وَإِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبُّكَ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱئْتِ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
- 26:11 قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ ۚ أَلَا يَتَّقُونَ
- 26:12 قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
- 26:13 وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ
- 26:14 وَلَهُمْ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌۭ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
- 26:15 قَالَ كَلَّا ۖ فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ ۖ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ
- 26:16 فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 26:17 أَنْ أَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
- 26:18 قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًۭا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ
- 26:19 وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِى فَعَلْتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
- 26:20 قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذًۭا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
- 26:21 فَفَرَرْتُ مِنكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِى رَبِّى حُكْمًۭا وَجَعَلَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
- 26:22 وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌۭ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَىَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
- 26:23 قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 26:24 قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ ۖ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ
- 26:25 قَالَ لِمَنْ حَوْلَهُۥٓ أَلَا تَسْتَمِعُونَ
- 26:26 قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ ءَابَآئِكُمُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
- 26:27 قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌۭ
- 26:28 قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ ۖ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
- 26:29 قَالَ لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذْتَ إِلَٰهًا غَيْرِى لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمَسْجُونِينَ
- 26:30 قَالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَىْءٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
- 26:31 قَالَ فَأْتِ بِهِۦٓ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
- 26:32 فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
- 26:33 وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ
- 26:34 قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌۭ
- 26:35 يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ
- 26:36 قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
- 26:37 يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَحَّارٍ عَلِيمٍۢ
- 26:38 فَجُمِعَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ لِمِيقَٰتِ يَوْمٍۢ مَّعْلُومٍۢ
- 26:39 وَقِيلَ لِلنَّاسِ هَلْ أَنتُم مُّجْتَمِعُونَ
- 26:40 لَعَلَّنَا نَتَّبِعُ ٱلسَّحَرَةَ إِن كَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
- 26:41 فَلَمَّا جَآءَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ قَالُوا۟ لِفِرْعَوْنَ أَئِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
- 26:42 قَالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنَّكُمْ إِذًۭا لَّمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ
- 26:43 قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰٓ أَلْقُوا۟ مَآ أَنتُم مُّلْقُونَ
- 26:44 فَأَلْقَوْا۟ حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا۟ بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
- 26:45 فَأَلْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ
- 26:46 فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سَٰجِدِينَ
- 26:47 قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 26:48 رَبِّ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ
- 26:49 قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ ۚ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍۢ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
- 26:50 قَالُوا۟ لَا ضَيْرَ ۖ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ
- 26:51 إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَآ أَن كُنَّآ أَوَّلَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:52 ۞ وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِىٓ إِنَّكُم مُّتَّبَعُونَ
- 26:53 فَأَرْسَلَ فِرْعَوْنُ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
- 26:54 إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌۭ قَلِيلُونَ
- 26:55 وَإِنَّهُمْ لَنَا لَغَآئِظُونَ
- 26:56 وَإِنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَٰذِرُونَ
- 26:57 فَأَخْرَجْنَٰهُم مِّن جَنَّٰتٍۢ وَعُيُونٍۢ
- 26:58 وَكُنُوزٍۢ وَمَقَامٍۢ كَرِيمٍۢ
- 26:59 كَذَٰلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْنَٰهَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
- 26:60 فَأَتْبَعُوهُم مُّشْرِقِينَ
- 26:61 فَلَمَّا تَرَٰٓءَا ٱلْجَمْعَانِ قَالَ أَصْحَٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ
- 26:62 قَالَ كَلَّآ ۖ إِنَّ مَعِىَ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ
- 26:63 فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْبَحْرَ ۖ فَٱنفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍۢ كَٱلطَّوْدِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
- 26:64 وَأَزْلَفْنَا ثَمَّ ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
- 26:65 وَأَنجَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥٓ أَجْمَعِينَ
- 26:66 ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
- 26:67 إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:68 وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
- 26:69 وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
- 26:70 إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ
- 26:71 قَالُوا۟ نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًۭا فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَٰكِفِينَ
- 26:72 قَالَ هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ إِذْ تَدْعُونَ
- 26:73 أَوْ يَنفَعُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَضُرُّونَ
- 26:74 قَالُوا۟ بَلْ وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا كَذَٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ
- 26:75 قَالَ أَفَرَءَيْتُم مَّا كُنتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ
- 26:76 أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُمُ ٱلْأَقْدَمُونَ
- 26:77 فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّۭ لِّىٓ إِلَّا رَبَّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 26:78 ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَنِى فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ
- 26:79 وَٱلَّذِى هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِى وَيَسْقِينِ
- 26:80 وَإِذَا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ
- 26:81 وَٱلَّذِى يُمِيتُنِى ثُمَّ يُحْيِينِ
- 26:82 وَٱلَّذِىٓ أَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لِى خَطِيٓـَٔتِى يَوْمَ ٱلدِّينِ
- 26:83 رَبِّ هَبْ لِى حُكْمًۭا وَأَلْحِقْنِى بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
- 26:84 وَٱجْعَل لِّى لِسَانَ صِدْقٍۢ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
- 26:85 وَٱجْعَلْنِى مِن وَرَثَةِ جَنَّةِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
- 26:86 وَٱغْفِرْ لِأَبِىٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
- 26:87 وَلَا تُخْزِنِى يَوْمَ يُبْعَثُونَ
- 26:88 يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالٌۭ وَلَا بَنُونَ
- 26:89 إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى ٱللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍۢ سَلِيمٍۢ
- 26:90 وَأُزْلِفَتِ ٱلْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
- 26:91 وَبُرِّزَتِ ٱلْجَحِيمُ لِلْغَاوِينَ
- 26:92 وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ
- 26:93 مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ هَلْ يَنصُرُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَنتَصِرُونَ
- 26:94 فَكُبْكِبُوا۟ فِيهَا هُمْ وَٱلْغَاوُۥنَ
- 26:95 وَجُنُودُ إِبْلِيسَ أَجْمَعُونَ
- 26:96 قَالُوا۟ وَهُمْ فِيهَا يَخْتَصِمُونَ
- 26:97 تَٱللَّهِ إِن كُنَّا لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍ
- 26:98 إِذْ نُسَوِّيكُم بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 26:99 وَمَآ أَضَلَّنَآ إِلَّا ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ
- 26:100 فَمَا لَنَا مِن شَٰفِعِينَ
- 26:101 وَلَا صَدِيقٍ حَمِيمٍۢ
- 26:102 فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةًۭ فَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:103 إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:104 وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
- 26:105 كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
- 26:106 إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ نُوحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
- 26:107 إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
- 26:108 فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
- 26:109 وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 26:110 فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
- 26:111 ۞ قَالُوٓا۟ أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ وَٱتَّبَعَكَ ٱلْأَرْذَلُونَ
- 26:112 قَالَ وَمَا عِلْمِى بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
- 26:113 إِنْ حِسَابُهُمْ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّى ۖ لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ
- 26:114 وَمَآ أَنَا۠ بِطَارِدِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:115 إِنْ أَنَا۠ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
- 26:116 قَالُوا۟ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ يَٰنُوحُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمَرْجُومِينَ
- 26:117 قَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِى كَذَّبُونِ
- 26:118 فَٱفْتَحْ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحًۭا وَنَجِّنِى وَمَن مَّعِىَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:119 فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ
- 26:120 ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا بَعْدُ ٱلْبَاقِينَ
- 26:121 إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:122 وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
- 26:123 كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
- 26:124 إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ هُودٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
- 26:125 إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
- 26:126 فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
- 26:127 وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 26:128 أَتَبْنُونَ بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ ءَايَةًۭ تَعْبَثُونَ
- 26:129 وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصَانِعَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَخْلُدُونَ
- 26:130 وَإِذَا بَطَشْتُم بَطَشْتُمْ جَبَّارِينَ
- 26:131 فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
- 26:132 وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَمَدَّكُم بِمَا تَعْلَمُونَ
- 26:133 أَمَدَّكُم بِأَنْعَٰمٍۢ وَبَنِينَ
- 26:134 وَجَنَّٰتٍۢ وَعُيُونٍ
- 26:135 إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍۢ
- 26:136 قَالُوا۟ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْنَآ أَوَعَظْتَ أَمْ لَمْ تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْوَٰعِظِينَ
- 26:137 إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا خُلُقُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
- 26:138 وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ
- 26:139 فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَهْلَكْنَٰهُمْ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:140 وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
- 26:141 كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
- 26:142 إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ صَٰلِحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
- 26:143 إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
- 26:144 فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
- 26:145 وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 26:146 أَتُتْرَكُونَ فِى مَا هَٰهُنَآ ءَامِنِينَ
- 26:147 فِى جَنَّٰتٍۢ وَعُيُونٍۢ
- 26:148 وَزُرُوعٍۢ وَنَخْلٍۢ طَلْعُهَا هَضِيمٌۭ
- 26:149 وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًۭا فَٰرِهِينَ
- 26:150 فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
- 26:151 وَلَا تُطِيعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ
- 26:152 ٱلَّذِينَ يُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ
- 26:153 قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَحَّرِينَ
- 26:154 مَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌۭ مِّثْلُنَا فَأْتِ بِـَٔايَةٍ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
- 26:155 قَالَ هَٰذِهِۦ نَاقَةٌۭ لَّهَا شِرْبٌۭ وَلَكُمْ شِرْبُ يَوْمٍۢ مَّعْلُومٍۢ
- 26:156 وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوٓءٍۢ فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍۢ
- 26:157 فَعَقَرُوهَا فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ نَٰدِمِينَ
- 26:158 فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:159 وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
- 26:160 كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
- 26:161 إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ لُوطٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
- 26:162 إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
- 26:163 فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
- 26:164 وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 26:165 أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلذُّكْرَانَ مِنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 26:166 وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم ۚ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ عَادُونَ
- 26:167 قَالُوا۟ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ يَٰلُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْرَجِينَ
- 26:168 قَالَ إِنِّى لِعَمَلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلْقَالِينَ
- 26:169 رَبِّ نَجِّنِى وَأَهْلِى مِمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ
- 26:170 فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ أَجْمَعِينَ
- 26:171 إِلَّا عَجُوزًۭا فِى ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ
- 26:172 ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
- 26:173 وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًۭا ۖ فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
- 26:174 إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:175 وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
- 26:176 كَذَّبَ أَصْحَٰبُ لْـَٔيْكَةِ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
- 26:177 إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ شُعَيْبٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
- 26:178 إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
- 26:179 فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
- 26:180 وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 26:181 ۞ أَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ وَلَا تَكُونُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْسِرِينَ
- 26:182 وَزِنُوا۟ بِٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ
- 26:183 وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا۟ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشْيَآءَهُمْ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ
- 26:184 وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُمْ وَٱلْجِبِلَّةَ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
- 26:185 قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَحَّرِينَ
- 26:186 وَمَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌۭ مِّثْلُنَا وَإِن نَّظُنُّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
- 26:187 فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًۭا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
- 26:188 قَالَ رَبِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
- 26:189 فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمِ ٱلظُّلَّةِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
- 26:190 إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:191 وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
- 26:192 وَإِنَّهُۥ لَتَنزِيلُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 26:193 نَزَلَ بِهِ ٱلرُّوحُ ٱلْأَمِينُ
- 26:194 عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنذِرِينَ
- 26:195 بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِىٍّۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
- 26:196 وَإِنَّهُۥ لَفِى زُبُرِ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
- 26:197 أَوَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُمْ ءَايَةً أَن يَعْلَمَهُۥ عُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
- 26:198 وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَٰهُ عَلَىٰ بَعْضِ ٱلْأَعْجَمِينَ
- 26:199 فَقَرَأَهُۥ عَلَيْهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ مُؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:200 كَذَٰلِكَ سَلَكْنَٰهُ فِى قُلُوبِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
- 26:201 لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَلِيمَ
- 26:202 فَيَأْتِيَهُم بَغْتَةًۭ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
- 26:203 فَيَقُولُوا۟ هَلْ نَحْنُ مُنظَرُونَ
- 26:204 أَفَبِعَذَابِنَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
- 26:205 أَفَرَءَيْتَ إِن مَّتَّعْنَٰهُمْ سِنِينَ
- 26:206 ثُمَّ جَآءَهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يُوعَدُونَ
- 26:207 مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يُمَتَّعُونَ
- 26:208 وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلَّا لَهَا مُنذِرُونَ
- 26:209 ذِكْرَىٰ وَمَا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
- 26:210 وَمَا تَنَزَّلَتْ بِهِ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ
- 26:211 وَمَا يَنۢبَغِى لَهُمْ وَمَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ
- 26:212 إِنَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّمْعِ لَمَعْزُولُونَ
- 26:213 فَلَا تَدْعُ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُعَذَّبِينَ
- 26:214 وَأَنذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ ٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ
- 26:215 وَٱخْفِضْ جَنَاحَكَ لِمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 26:216 فَإِنْ عَصَوْكَ فَقُلْ إِنِّى بَرِىٓءٌۭ مِّمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
- 26:217 وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
- 26:218 ٱلَّذِى يَرَىٰكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ
- 26:219 وَتَقَلُّبَكَ فِى ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ
- 26:220 إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
- 26:221 هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن تَنَزَّلُ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ
- 26:222 تَنَزَّلُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍۢ
- 26:223 يُلْقُونَ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ كَٰذِبُونَ
- 26:224 وَٱلشُّعَرَآءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ ٱلْغَاوُۥنَ
- 26:225 أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِى كُلِّ وَادٍۢ يَهِيمُونَ
- 26:226 وَأَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ مَا لَا يَفْعَلُونَ
- 26:227 إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَذَكَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًۭا وَٱنتَصَرُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُوا۟ ۗ وَسَيَعْلَمُ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَىَّ مُنقَلَبٍۢ يَنقَلِبُونَ


===== _commentary/v16/work/s026/surah.r2/dictionary.md =====
# Dictionary: every branch of every focus root

Every root of the surah's words, each once, headed by the ayah and word where it first occurs; it also serves the later words listed with it.
One entry per branch: a Turkish label and Turkish glosses of its attested senses, then the classical dictionaries' own phrases with their source tags (ayn, sihah, tahdhib, maqayis, mufradat, jamhara). [kalıp] marks a sense the dictionaries attest only inside a fixed expression.
Identity roots come from the quran-data gateway. Word-scoped alternatives are cited analyses of this
exact word. **Echo roots** are observed but withheld mappings: sound-family candidates, not identity.

  قطعته قطعا ومقطعا فانقطع؛ الأقطع المقطوع اليد (ayn)؛ قطعت الشئ قطعا؛ الأقطع المقطوع اليد (sihah)؛ القطع مصدر قطعت؛ وقطعن أيديهن أي قطعنها قطعا بعد قطع وخدشن فيها خدوشا كثيرة (tahdhib)؛ القطع فصل الشيء مدركا بالبصر كالأجسام؛ قطع الأعضاء؛ فقطع أمعاءهم (mufradat)؛ يدل على صرم وإبانة شيء من شيء؛ قطعت الشيء أقطعه قطعا (maqayis)
- **B002** ayrılmış parça — ayrılmış bölüm veya parça · gecenin bir bölümü
  القطعة طائفة من كل شيء؛ قطعة أرضي (ayn)؛ القطعة من الشئ الطائفة منه؛ قطعة من الأرض إذا كانت مفروزة (sihah)؛ اسم ما قطع فسقط قطع؛ أعطني قطعة؛ قطعة من أرض؛ المقطع الشيء اليسير منه (tahdhib)؛ قطع من الليل قطعة منه (mufradat)؛ القطع الطائفة من الليل كأنه قطعة؛ أقطعت الرجل إقطاعا كأنه طائفة قد قطعت من بلد (maqayis)
- **B003** kat edip geçmek [kalıp] — nehri veya suyu geçmek · yolda ilerleyip yolu kat etmek
  قطعت النهر قطوعا (ayn)؛ قطعت النهر قطوعا عبرته؛ مقاطع الأنهار حيث تعبر فيه (sihah)؛ قطعت النهر قطعا وقطوعا؛ المقطع الموضع الذي يقطع فيه النهر من المعابر (tahdhib)؛ قطع الطريق يراد به السير والسلوك؛ قطع الماء بالسباحة عبوره (mufradat)؛ قطعت النهر قطوعا إذا عبرته (maqayis)
- **B004** kuşların göç etmesi [kalıp] — kuşların bir bölgeden başka bölgeye gitmesi · gidip dönen kuşlar
  الطير تقطع في طيرانها قطوعا وهن قواطع أي ذواهب ورواجع (ayn)؛ قطعت الطير قطوعا وقطاعا خرجت من بلاد البرد إلى بلاد الحر فهي قواطع ذواهب أو رواجع (sihah)؛ قطعت الطير تقطع قطوعا إذا جاءت من بلد إلى بلد في وقت حر أو برد؛ قطعت الغربان إلينا في الشتاء قطوعا (tahdhib)؛ قطعت الطير قطوعا إذا خرجت من بلاد البرد إلى بلاد الحر أو من تلك إلى هذه (maqayis)
- **B005** sona erip kesilmek — bir şeyin zamanı veya varlığı bitmek · bir şeyin sona erdiği yer · kuyu suyunun azalması veya tükenmesi
  منقطع كل شيء حيث تنتهي غايته؛ انقطع الشيء ذهب وقته؛ انقطع البرد والحر (ayn)؛ قطع ماء الركية أي انقطع وذهب؛ منقطع الرمل حيث ينقطع ولا رمل خلفه؛ منقطع كل شيء حيث ينتهى إليه طرفه (sihah)؛ منقطع كل شيء حيث ينقطع مثل منقطع الرمل والحرة؛ أقطعت السماء إذا انقطع المطر؛ قطع ماء قليبكم إذا قل ماؤها وذهب (tahdhib)؛ أصاب بئرهم قطع أي انقطع ماؤها؛ مقاطع الأودية مآخيرها (mufradat)؛ منقطع الرمل ومقطعه حيث ينقطع؛ أصاب بئر فلان قطع إذا نقص ماؤها (maqayis)
- **B006** umudu kesilmek veya yolda kalmak [kalıp] — umudu kesilmek veya yolculukta kalmak · yolculuğu sürdüremeyen kimse
  قطع بفلان انقطع رجاؤه؛ رجل منقطع به؛ عجز عن سفره من نفقة ذهبت أو قامت عليه راحلته (ayn)؛ قطع بفلان فهو مقطوع به؛ انقطع به فهو منقطع به إذا عجز عن سفره (sihah)؛ قطع بالرجل إذا انقطع رجاؤه؛ رجل منقطع به إذا كان مسافرا فأبدع به وعطبت راحلته وذهب زاده وماله؛ أقطع عن أهله فهو مقطع عنهم (tahdhib)؛ لليائس من الشيء قد قطع به كأنه أمل أمله فانقطع (maqayis)
- **B007** bağı koparmak — ilişkiyi bırakma ve bağ kopukluğu · kopuşu bildiren işaret · akrabalık bağını ve iyiliği kesmek
  قاطع الرحم؛ قطع رحمه إذا هجرها؛ الأقطوعة علامة أنها صارمتها؛ الهجر مقطعة للود (ayn)؛ قطع رحمه قطيعة؛ رحم قطعاء؛ الأقطوعة علامة للصريمة والهجران؛ التقاطع ضد التواصل (sihah)؛ تقطعت أسبابهم ووصلهم؛ قطعت حبال مودتها؛ قطع فلان رحمه؛ اتقوا القطيعاء أي أن ينقطع بعضكم من بعض في الحرب (tahdhib)؛ قطع الوصل هو الهجران؛ قطع الرحم يكون بالهجران ومنع البر (mufradat)؛ القطيعة الهجران؛ تقاطع الرجلان إذا تصارما؛ أقطوعة علامة للصريمة (maqayis)
- **B008** bölüp dağıtmak [kalıp] — işlerini kendi aralarında bölüp ayırmak · onları yeryüzünde gruplara ayırmak · topluluğun dağılıp ayrılması
  قطعت عليه العذاب تقطيعا أي لونته وجزأته عليه (ayn)؛ تقطعوا أمرهم بينهم أي تقسموه (sihah)؛ قطعناهم في الأرض أمما أي فرقناهم فرقا؛ فتقطعوا أمرهم بينهم زبرا؛ قطع فلان على فلان العذاب إذا لون عليه ضروبا (tahdhib)؛ تقضع القوم تفرقوا وهذا من الإبدال أيضا (maqayis ibdal)
- **B009** iple boğulmak [kalıp] — iple boğulmak
  قطع الرجل بحبل أي اختنق؛ ثم ليقطع أي ليختنق (ayn)؛ ثم ليقطع قالوا ليختنق؛ يقطع نفسه من الأرض حتى يختنق (sihah)؛ أجمع المفسرون على أن تأويل ثم ليقطع ثم ليختنق؛ يقطع حياته ونفسه خنقا (tahdhib)؛ ليقطع أجله بالاختناق؛ ثم ليختنق (mufradat)؛ في قوله ثم ليقطع إنه الاختناق (maqayis)
- **B010** kesin karara bağlamak [kalıp] — işi kesinleştirip sonuca bağlamak · hakkın yanlıştan ayrıldığı karar noktası
  مقطع الحق موضع التقاء الحكم فيه وهو ما يفصل الحق من الباطل (ayn)؛ مقطع الحق حيث يفصل بين الخصوم بنص الحكم (tahdhib)؛ قطع الأمر فصله؛ ما كنت قاطعة أمرا (mufradat)
- **B011** kökünü kazımak [kalıp] — bir soyun devamını yok etmek · bir topluluğun bir bölümünü yok etmek
  ليقطع طرفا أي يهلك جماعة منهم؛ قطع دابر الإنسان هو إفناء نوعه؛ إلا أن تقطع قلوبهم أي إلا أن يموتوا وقيل إلا أن يتوبوا توبة بها تنقطع قلوبهم ندما
- **B012** giysi biçip dikmek [kalıp] — onlara giysi biçip dikildi · biçilmiş veya kısa giysiler · kumaşın gömlek olmaya yetmesi
  المقطعات من الثياب شبه الجباب؛ الثياب المختلفة الألوان؛ القطع من الثياب ضرب منها (ayn)؛ المقطعات من الثياب شبه الجباب؛ مقطعات الثياب والشعر قصارها؛ هذا الثوب يقطعك قميصا (sihah)؛ قطعت لهم ثياب من نار أي خيطت وسويت وجعلت لبوسا؛ المقطعات من الثياب كل ثوب يقطع من قميص وغيره؛ الثوب يقطعك قميصا (tahdhib)؛ قطع الثوب؛ قطعت لهم ثياب من نار (mufradat)؛ هذا الثوب يقطعك قميصا؛ المقطعات الثياب القصار (maqayis)
- **B013** pay ayırıp vermek [kalıp] — valinin araziden pay vermesi · dalları kesmeme izin verdi · bir şeyden bölüm ayırıp almak
  أقطع الوالي قطيعة أي طائفة من أرض الخراج؛ أقطعني قضبانا أذن لي قطعها؛ أقطع فلان من مال فلان طائفة (ayn)؛ أقطعته قضبانا أي أذنت له في قطعها؛ أقطعته قطيعة أي طائفة من أرض الخراج؛ اقتطعت قطيعا من غنم فلان (sihah)؛ أقطعني فلان نهرا إذا أذن له في حفره؛ أقطعني قضبانا من كرمه؛ قاطعت فلانا على كذا من الأجر والعمل (tahdhib)؛ أقطعت الرجل إقطاعا كأنه طائفة قد قطعت من بلد؛ أقطعت فلانا قضبانا من الكرم إذا أذنت له في قطعها (maqayis)
- **B014** kesici alet — kesmeye yarayan alet · keskin kılıç · kısa enli ok ucu
  المقطع كل شيء يقطع به؛ قاطع فلان وفلان سيفيهما أي نظرا أيهما أقطع؛ القطع نصل صغير يجعل في السهم (ayn)؛ المقطع ما يقطع به الشئ؛ القطع نصل قصير عريض السهم (sihah)؛ سيف قاطع وقطاع ومقطع؛ كل شيء يقطع به فهو مقطع؛ القطاع لا القاطع؛ القطع من النصال القصير العريض (tahdhib)؛ القطع النصل من السهام العريض كأنه لما بري قطع (maqayis)
- **B015** kesilmiş donatı nesnesi — kesik uçlu veya şeritlerden yapılmış kamçı · eyer altına serilen yaygı
  القطيع السوط المقطوع طرفه؛ القطع من الثياب ضرب منها (ayn)؛ القطع طنفسة يجعلها الراكب تحته؛ القطيع السوط (sihah)؛ القطع طنفسة تكون تحت الرحل؛ القطيع السوط المتقطع؛ سمي قطيعا لأنه يقطع أربع طاقات ثم يلوي (tahdhib)؛ القطيع السوط؛ القطع الطنفسة تلقى على الرحل وكأنها سميت بذلك لأن ناسجها يقطعها من غيرها (maqayis)
- **B016** hayvan sürüsü [kalıp] — koyun veya benzeri hayvan sürüsü
  القطيع طائفة من الغنم والنعم ونحوها (ayn)؛ القطيع الطائفة من البقر والغنم؛ اقتطعت قطيعا من غنم فلان (sihah)؛ القطيع من الغنم جمعه قطعان كالصرمة والفرقة (mufradat)؛ القطيع القطعة من الغنم (maqayis)
- **B017** hızla geride bırakmak — atın diğer atları geçip geride bırakması · çok hızlı tavşan · hızlı hızlı ardı ardına gelenler
  الفرس الجواد يقطع الخيل إذا خلفها ومضى؛ الأرنب السريعة مقطعة النياط؛ جاءت الخيل مقطوطعات أي سراعا بعضها في إثر بعض (ayn)؛ قطع الفرس الخيل تقطيعا أي خلفها ومضى؛ جاءت الخيل مقطوطعات أي سراعا بعضها في إثر بعض (sihah)؛ يقال للأرنب السريعة مقطعة النياط ومقطعة الأسحار؛ الفرس الجواد يقطع الخيل تقطيعا؛ ليس فيكم من تقطع عليه الأعناق مثل أبي بكر (tahdhib)؛ مقطعة النياط الأرنب؛ قطع الفرس الخيل تقطيعا خلفها ومضى؛ جاءت الخيل مقطوطعات أي سراعا (maqayis)
- **B018** benzersiz olmak [kalıp] — belirli nitelikte eşi benzeri olmayan · kötülükte dizginsiz olan
  منقطع القرين في الكرم والسخاء إذا لم يكن له مثل؛ منقطع العقال في الشر والخبث (ayn)؛ فلان منقطع القرين في سخاء أو غيره (sihah)؛ فلان منقطع القرين إذا لم يكن له مثل في سخاء أو فضل (tahdhib)؛ فلان منقطع القرين في سخاء أو غيره (maqayis)
- **B019** yapıca benzer olmak [kalıp] — birine boy ve yapı bakımından benzeyen · düzgün ve güzel beden yapısı
  القطيع شبه النظير؛ هذا قطيع هذا أي شبهه في خلقه وقده؛ حسن التقطيع أي القد (ayn)؛ فلان قطيع فلان أي شبيهه في قده وخلقه؛ شيء حسن التقطيع إذا كان حسن القد (tahdhib)
- **B020** gücü kesilmek [kalıp] — zayıflık veya ağırlık yüzünden kalkamaz olan · cinsel eyleme güç yetiremeyen veya istemeyen · susturulup cevap veremeyen
  أقطع ضعف عن النكاح؛ قطيع القيام أي منقطع إذا أراد القيام من ثقل أو سمنة وربما من شدة ضعفه (ayn)؛ فلان قطيع القيام إذا وصف بالضعف أو السمن؛ أقطع الرجل إذا انقطعت حجته وبكتوه بالحق فلم يجب (sihah)؛ رجل قطيع القيام إذا كان ضعيفا؛ أقطع الرجل إذا لم يرد النساء؛ أقطع كلام الرجل إذا بكتوه بالحق فلم يقدر على الجواب (tahdhib)؛ جارية قطيع القيام كأنها من سمنها تنقطع عنه (maqayis)
- **B021** iç sancı, nefes sıkışması veya iç kopma — karın veya bağırsakta sancı · soluk daralması ve yüksek nefes · içinde damar veya yağ kopmuş olan
  التقطيع مغس تجده في الأمعاء؛ القطع بهر يأخذ الفرس؛ إن انقطع عرق في بطنه أو مشحمه فهو مقطوع (ayn)؛ أصابه قطع أي بهر؛ التقطيع مغص في البطن (sihah)؛ التقطيع مغص يجده الإنسان في بطنه وأمعائه؛ القطع البهر؛ الفرس أيضا يأخذه القطع؛ إذا انقطع عرق في بطنه أو شحم فهو مقطوع (tahdhib)؛ القطع البهر (maqayis)
- **B022** sözü veya şiiri bölmek [kalıp] — dil çevikliği gitmiş veya az konuşan · belirli ağızda kelime sonunu düşürme · şiiri ölçü parçalarına ayırma · kısa şiir parçaları
  قطيع اللسان إذا ذهبت السلاطة منه؛ القطعة في طيء أن يقول يا أبا الحكا وهو يريد يا أبا الحكم؛ المقطعات من الشعر والأراحيز (ayn)؛ تقطيع الشعر وزنه بأجزاء العروض؛ مقطعات الثياب والشعر قصارها (sihah)؛ امرأة قطيع الكلام إذا لم تكن سليطة؛ تقطيع البيت في بيوت الشعر تجزئته بالأفعال؛ القطعة في طيء كالعنعنة في تميم (tahdhib)
- **B023** yol kesmek [kalıp] — yolcuları durdurup soyan kimseler
  قطاع الطرق الذين يعارضون أبناء السبيل فيقطعون بهم الطريق (tahdhib)؛ قطع الطريق يقال على وجهين؛ الثاني يراد به الغصب من المارة والسالكين للطريق؛ يؤدي إلى انقطاع الناس عن الطريق (mufradat)
- **B024** şartlı anlaşmak [kalıp] — bir kimseyle belirli iş veya ödeme üzerinde anlaşmak
  قاطعته على كذا (sihah)؛ قاطعت فلانا على كذا وكذا من الأجر والعمل مقاطعة (tahdhib)

## ر ج ل (root_000546): 26:49 وَأَرْجُلَكُم

- **B001** bacak uzvu — insan veya hayvanın bacak uzvu · koyunu bacağından asmak · kişiyi bacağından yakalamak · iri bacaklı
  الرجل رجل الإنسان وغيره (maqayis)؛ الرجل واحدة الأرجل (sihah)؛ الرجل العضو المخصوص بأكثر الحيوان (mufradat)؛ رجلت الشاة علقتها برجلها (maqayis;sihah)؛ ارتجلت الرجل أخذت برجله (maqayis;sihah)؛ الأرجل العظيم الرجل (maqayis;ayn;sihah)
- **B002** erkek insan — kadın olmayan erkek insan · bazı özellikleriyle erkeğe benzetilen kadın · erkekçe olgunluk ve dayanıklılık
  هذا رجل أي ليس بأنثى (ayn)؛ الرجل خلاف المرأة (sihah)؛ الرجل مختص بالذكر من الناس (mufradat)؛ الرجولية والجلادة (mufradat)؛ يقال للمرأة الرجلة (maqayis;sihah)
- **B003** yaya giden kişi — yaya giden, binici olmayan kişi · yayalar topluluğu · yürümeye güçlü ve dayanıklı kimse · yürünmesi güç, çok taşlı arazi · bineğinden inip yaya olmak
  الرجل الرجالة (maqayis)؛ هذا رجل أي راجل (ayn)؛ الرجل خلاف الفارس (sihah)؛ اشتق من الرجل رجل وراجل للماشي بالرجل (mufradat)؛ رجل رجيل أي قوي على المشى (sihah)؛ ترجل القوم نزلوا على دوابهم (ayn)؛ حرة رجلاء يصعب فيها المشي (jamhara)
- **B004** birinin devrinde [kalıp] — belirtilen kişinin devrinde ve zamanında
  كان ذاك على رجل فلان أي في زمانه (maqayis)؛ كان ذلك على رجل فلان أي في عهده وزمانه (sihah)؛ استعير الرجل لزمان الإنسان (mufradat)
- **B005** bir bacağı beyaz hayvan [kalıp] — bir bacağında beyazlık bulunan at veya başka bir hayvan
  الأرجل من الدواب الذي ابيض أحد رجليه (maqayis)؛ الرجلة أيضا مصدر الأرجل من الدواب بإحدى رجليه بياض (ayn)؛ فرس أرجل والأنثى رجلاء إذا كان في إحدى رجليه بياض (jamhara)؛ الأرجل من الخيل الذي في إحدى رجليه بياض (sihah)؛ الأرجل الأبيض الرجل من الفرس (mufradat)
- **B006** büyük çekirge sürüsü [kalıp] — büyük çekirge kümesi veya sürüsü
  الرجل القطيع من الجراد ونحوه من الخلق (ayn)؛ رأيت رجلا من جراد أي قطعة عظيمة (jamhara)؛ الرجل أيضا الجماعة الكثيرة من الجراد خاصة (sihah)؛ استعير الرجل للقطعة من الجراد (mufradat)
- **B007** semizotu diye bilinen ot — semizotu diye anılan ot; bazı tanıklıklarda tuzcul bitki · kereviz
  الرجلة هي التي يقال لها البقلة الحمقاء (maqayis)؛ الرجلة منبت العرفج الكثير (ayn)؛ التراجيل الكرفس (ayn)؛ الرجلة نبت من الحمض (jamhara)؛ الرجلة بقلة وتسمى الحمقاء (sihah)؛ الرجلة البقلة الحمقاء (mufradat)
- **B008** su akıntısı yatağı [kalıp] — suyun aktığı tek bir doğal yol veya yatak
  قال قوم بل الرجل مسايل الماء واحدتها رجلة (maqayis)؛ الرجلة أيضا واحدة الرجل وهي مسايل الماء (sihah)؛ استعير الرجل لمسيل الماء الواحدة رجلة (mufradat)

  العاشق الهيمان كأنه جن من العشق فذهب على وجهه على غير قصد (maqayis)؛ الهائم المتحير هام يهيم؛ الهيام كالجنون من العشق (ayn)؛ هام على وجهه يهيم هيما وهيمانا ذهب من العشق أو غيره؛ قلب مستهام (sihah)؛ إذا أحب المرأة؛ الهيام العشاق؛ الهيام الموسوسون؛ الهيوم أن يذهب على وجهه؛ الهائم المتحير؛ الهيام كالجنون من العشق (tahdhib)؛ استهيم فؤاده؛ الهيم هيمان العاشق؛ الشاعر إذا خلا في الصحراء هام؛ وادي الكلام (tahdhib)؛ هام على وجهه ذهب؛ في كل نوع من الكلام يغلون؛ المخالف للقصد الذاهب على وجهه؛ اشتد عشقه (mufradat)

(source: latent_activation/network/v3/reviews/s026/reader_a_pilot.md)

# s026 Semantic Channel Discovery

## Parent Channels

### 1. Disclosure Made Perceptible (P1, 26:1-20)
- Semantic invariant: A message hidden in source or medium becomes an inspectable sign, intelligible statement, or audible summons.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:2-6 presents signs, a clear book, renewed reminder, denial, and arriving news, while 26:10-17 turns disclosure into a call and commissioned speech.
- Surprising reach: The lexical field makes revelation simultaneously inscription, evidentiary document, emergence into clarity, and voiced dispatch.

#### Subchannel A. Inscribed and Evidentiary Disclosure
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A written object bears signs whose meaning emerges clearly and whose renewed presentation functions like documentary evidence.
- Active motifs: written artifact (`quranic:root_001283:B002/m01`); visible sign (`quranic:root_000074:B003/m01`); emergence into clarity (`quranic:root_000170:B004/m01`); meaning disclosed by sign or writing (`quranic:root_000170:B005/m01`); right-bearing document (`quranic:root_000516:B008/m01`); renewed report (`quranic:root_000299:B003/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:2 `ءايت`, `الكتب`, `المبين`; 26:4 `ءاية`; 26:5 `ذكر`, `محدث`
- Synthesis: The clear book is not merely a container of propositions. Its signs materialize disclosure as something written, made visible, and brought out of obscurity. The latent documentary sense of `ذكر` sharpens the reminder into a warrant that can stand against denial, while `محدث` supplies the recurring event of its presentation.

#### Subchannel B. Voiced Dispatch and Reception
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A raised call initiates a dispatch whose message travels through tongue and messenger toward hearing and eventual report.
- Active motifs: raised call (`quranic:root_001486:B002/m01`); sending or releasing (`quranic:root_000563:B001/m01`); messenger and message (`quranic:root_000563:B002/m01`); articulated tongue (`quranic:root_001355:B001/m01`); relayed communication (`quranic:root_001355:B008/m01`); auditory reception (`quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`); responsive hearing (`quranic:root_000741:B003/m01`); arriving report (`quranic:root_001464:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:6 `انبؤا`; 26:10 `نادى`; 26:13 `لسانى`, `فارسل`; 26:15 `مستمعون`; 26:16 `رسول`; 26:17 `ارسل`
- Synthesis: The call to Moses unfolds as a transmission chain: summons, release, bearer, tongue, hearing, and report. The same scene pressures the primary reading by making failed reception part of the channel itself: an audible message has reached its audience even when responsive hearing does not follow.

### 2. Embodied Pressure and Release (P1, 26:1-20)
- Semantic invariant: Missionary resistance is registered in the body as depletion, lowered posture, constriction, and threatened injury, then countered by release into speech.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:3-4 pictures self-consuming grief and bowed necks, while 26:12-15 names fear, a constricted chest, an unfree tongue, threatened killing, and divine accompaniment.
- Surprising reach: Emotional and political pressure become anatomical mechanics, with breath, neck, chest, and tongue forming one pressure-and-release system.

#### Subchannel A. Self-Consuming Grief
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Unanswered concern exhausts the self as though grief were an act of bodily destruction.
- Active motifs: killing oneself from grief (`quranic:root_000088:B001/m01`); wasting exhaustion (`quranic:root_000088:B003/m01`); breath leaving the body (`quranic:root_001533:B001/m01`); relief after distress (`quranic:root_001533:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:3 `بخع`, `نفسك`
- Synthesis: `باخع نفسك` is amplified by the branch's exhaustion sense: concern for unbelief consumes vitality rather than remaining an abstract emotion. The same-root movement from the living self and breath toward relief keeps open the counter-image of a self restored after pressure.

#### Subchannel B. Lowered Neck and Constricted Chest
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: External compulsion bends the neck while anticipated rejection narrows the chest and threatens the neck with cutting.
- Active motifs: lowered neck or head (`quranic:root_000419:B002/m01`); neck as vulnerable member (`quranic:root_001053:B001/m01`); severing the neck bone (`quranic:root_000088:B004/m01`); chest as bodily cavity (`quranic:root_000849:B001/m01`); constriction of the chest (`quranic:root_000925:B002/m01`); fear before danger (`quranic:root_000447:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:3 `بخع`; 26:4 `اعنقهم`, `خضعين`; 26:12 `اخاف`; 26:13 `يضيق`, `صدرى`; 26:14 `اخاف`
- Synthesis: The hypothetical sign makes resistance collapse into bowed anatomy, whereas Moses experiences mission as inward narrowing. The latent neck-cutting sense links compelled submission to the explicit threat of killing, producing a tight bodily scene of vulnerability rather than a generic motif of fear.

#### Subchannel C. Speech Released from Restraint
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A tongue that does not move freely is released through shared commission and guaranteed hearing.
- Active motifs: release from a fetter (`quranic:root_000946:B001/m01`); unobstructed movement (`quranic:root_000946:B003/m01`); tongue as speech organ (`quranic:root_001355:B001/m01`); sending a delegate (`quranic:root_000563:B001/m01`); attentive hearing (`quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:13 `لا ينطلق`, `لسانى`, `فارسل`; 26:15 `مستمعون`
- Synthesis: The failure of the tongue to `ينطلق` is a restraint scene: speech cannot set out. Sending to Aaron and the promise of listening reverse that immobility, so delegated speech becomes the practical release of a bound communicative faculty.

### 3. Cultivation and Human Formation (P1, 26:1-20)
- Semantic invariant: Growth requires a receptive substrate, sustaining moisture, differentiation, and time, whether the product is vegetation or a formed human life.
- Surface relation: indirect; 26:7 explicitly shows earth producing noble pairs, while 26:9-10 and 26:18-19 activate latent rain, irrigation, nurture, age, and seed-covering senses.
- Surprising reach: Royal upbringing and prophetic emergence are reframed through an agricultural process in which cultivation does not guarantee ownership of the mature yield.

#### Subchannel A. Moist Earth, Planting, and Yield
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Soft earth receives planting, cloud and dew provide moisture, irrigation sustains it, and differentiated growth emerges as a valued yield.
- Active motifs: fertile soft earth (`quranic:root_000025:B002/m01`); plant emerging from earth (`quranic:root_001465:B001/m01`); deliberate planting (`quranic:root_001465:B002/m01`); raincloud (`quranic:root_000532:B008/m01`); dew or rain moisture (`quranic:root_001486:B003/m01`); irrigation device (`quranic:root_000751:B001/m01`); produced yield (`quranic:root_000009:B007/m01`); differentiated kind (`quranic:root_000652:B004/m01`); quality of plant and rain (`quranic:root_001294:B002/m01`); seed covered in soil (`quranic:root_001307:B008/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:5-6 `ياتيهم`; 26:7 `الارض`, `انبتنا`, `زوج`, `كريم`; 26:9 `ربك`; 26:10 `نادى`, `ربك`; 26:18 `سنين`; 26:19 `الكفرين`
- Synthesis: The visible earth-and-plant sign recruits latent senses from nearby roots into a complete cultivation scene. Lordship contributes raincloud, calling contributes dew, years contribute irrigation, arrival contributes yield, and disbelief contributes seed-covering. These are not parallel catalog items: together they materialize how a sign can be planted, sustained, differentiated, and still remain covered.

#### Subchannel B. Upbringing Across a Lifespan
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A child is nurtured within a household, grows through an extended stay, and is claimed through lineage and elapsed years.
- Active motifs: nurture and formative repair (`quranic:root_000532:B002/m01`); feeding that makes grow (`quranic:root_000537:B005/m01`); organic human growth (`quranic:root_001465:B006/m01`); child or offspring (`quranic:root_001683:B001/m01`); newborn under household power (`quranic:root_001683:B004/m01`); filial lineage (`quranic:root_000156:B007/m01`); measured lifespan (`quranic:root_001044:B001/m01`); prolonged remaining (`quranic:root_001339:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:7 `انبتنا`; 26:16 `رب`; 26:17 `بنى`; 26:18 `نربك`, `وليدا`, `لبثت`, `عمرك`, `سنين`
- Synthesis: Pharaoh's claim compresses nurture, household incorporation, residence, and age into a proprietary account of Moses' formation. The growth imagery usefully pressures that claim: cultivation can sustain a life, but the mature agent's commission and judgment are not reducible to the household that once fed him.

### 4. Rejection as Covering and Deflection (P1, 26:1-20)
- Semantic invariant: Resistance prevents a received sign from governing conduct by hiding, turning from, falsifying, or ridiculing it.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:5-6 describes turning away, denial, and mockery, and 26:12, 26:19-20 revisits accusation, covering, and acknowledged error.
- Surprising reach: Rejection operates less as a single belief-state than as a sequence of spatial and rhetorical evasions.

#### Subchannel A. Concealment and Turning Aside
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: What has arrived is covered over and the recipient presents a side rather than a receptive face.
- Active motifs: concealment of truth (`quranic:root_001307:B003/m01`); concealment of received favor (`quranic:root_001307:B004/m01`); turning or presenting the side (`quranic:root_001001:B005/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:5 `معرضين`; 26:19 `الكفرين`; 26:20 `الضالين`
- Synthesis: Covering and turning are distinct operations. The first obscures what is present; the second redirects the self away from it. Their conjunction makes disbelief a practiced deflection, while Moses' earlier `ضلال` remains a separable error of route rather than the same operation.

#### Subchannel B. Falsification and Ridicule
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A message is branded false, its bearer anticipates the same accusation, and delayed consequences become the object of ridicule.
- Active motifs: making a lie (`quranic:root_001290:B001/m01`); accusing another of lying (`quranic:root_001290:B002/m01`); mockery and derision (`quranic:root_001587:B001/m01`); attributing unsaid speech (`quranic:root_001272:B005/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:6 `كذبوا`, `يستهزءون`; 26:12 `يكذبون`; 26:18-20 `قال`
- Synthesis: Falsification acts on the status of the message, while ridicule acts on the relation between warning and outcome. The latent attribution sense of speech adds a rhetorical pressure point: rejection can manufacture a statement to dismiss rather than answer the one actually delivered.

### 5. Sovereign Control of Council and Bodies (P2, 26:21-51)
- Semantic invariant: Political sovereignty organizes deliberation, mobilizes crowds, assigns rank, and threatens coercive control over bodies.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:25, 26:34-42 stages court speech and public muster, and 26:29, 26:49 turns royal command into imprisonment and mutilation.
- Surprising reach: The same regime that choreographs collective attention also tries to fix belief spatially in prison and physically on crossed limbs.

#### Subchannel A. Court Deliberation
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A ruler addresses the surrounding elite, converts a sign into a security claim, and solicits a command through managed consultation.
- Active motifs: governing sovereignty (`quranic:root_000532:B001/m01`); elite council (`quranic:root_001441:B002/m01`); collusive council (`quranic:root_001441:B003/m01`); surrounding court (`quranic:root_000373:B004/m01`); binding command (`quranic:root_000051:B002/m01`); ruler's directive (`quranic:root_000051:B003/m01`); deliberative counsel (`quranic:root_000051:B007/m01`); negotiated speech (`quranic:root_001272:B009/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:23-28 `رب`; 26:25 `حوله`; 26:34 `للملا`, `حوله`; 26:35 `تامرون`; 26:34-36 `قال`
- Synthesis: Pharaoh does not answer the sign alone; he routes it through a council scene. The elite, surrounding space, command, and negotiated speech materialize how sovereignty manufactures a public interpretation before it mobilizes a response.

#### Subchannel B. Public Muster
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Agents are dispatched through cities to rouse skilled participants, gather them at a fixed time, and assemble an audience around a promised victory.
- Active motifs: rousing the stationary (`quranic:root_000129:B001/m01`); dispatching an agent (`quranic:root_000129:B002/m01`); mobilizing a troop (`quranic:root_000129:B004/m01`); driving a crowd toward one goal (`quranic:root_000324:B001/m01`); collecting dispersed people (`quranic:root_000259:B001/m01`); appointed gathering (`quranic:root_000259:B004/m01`); city as mobilization space (`quranic:root_001408:B001/m01`); fixed time (`quranic:root_001671:B003/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:36 `ابعث`, `المدائن`, `حشرين`; 26:38 `فجمع`, `لميقت`; 26:39 `مجتمعون`
- Synthesis: The contest is produced logistically before it is performed. Dispatch, urban collection, timed appointment, and audience formation create a directed crowd whose expected conclusion has already been politically framed.

#### Subchannel C. Captivity and Crosswise Mutilation
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Sovereign disagreement is answered by confinement, binding, severing paired limbs, and fixing bodies on a public support.
- Active motifs: prison confinement (`quranic:root_000678:B001/m01`); seizure and capture (`quranic:root_000018:B003/m01`); tethering restraint (`quranic:root_001036:B002/m01`); leg restraint (`quranic:root_001036:B009/m01`); rope as binding tool (`quranic:root_000291:B001/m01`); bodily severing (`quranic:root_001240:B001/m01`); partition into opposed sides (`quranic:root_001240:B008/m01`); cruciform fixing (`quranic:root_000875:B005/m01`); hand (`quranic:root_001693:B001/m01`); foot (`quranic:root_000546:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:28 `تعقلون`; 26:29 `المسجونين`; 26:44 `حبالهم`; 26:49 `لاقطعن`, `ايديكم`, `ارجلكم`, `خلف`, `لاصلبنكم`, `اجمعين`
- Synthesis: The threat translates dissent into a body-management procedure. Rope and restraint extend imprisonment; cutting turns paired limbs into opposed sides; crucifixion converts the punished body into a public sign. This coercive sign competes directly with the signs Pharaoh cannot control.

### 6. Materialized Contest of Signs (P2, 26:21-51)
- Semantic invariant: Rival claims become visible through handled implements, altered motion, and decisive consumption of fabricated effects.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:30-46 moves from a demanded clear thing to cast staves and ropes, a serpent, swallowing, and involuntary prostration.
- Surprising reach: False representation is defeated not by a verbal rebuttal but by an ingestive mechanism that removes its material performance.

#### Subchannel A. Cast Implements and Fabricated Motion
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Contestants cast ropes and staves into a shared field where tools of support and binding become instruments of visual diversion.
- Active motifs: forceful casting (`quranic:root_001372:B005/m01`); rope as implement (`quranic:root_000291:B001/m01`); rope as snare (`quranic:root_000291:B005/m01`); staff as support (`quranic:root_005713:B001/m01`); laying down the staff (`quranic:root_005713:B003/m01`); magical diversion (`quranic:root_000682:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:32 `فالقى`, `عصاه`; 26:34 `لسحر`; 26:43 `القوا`; 26:44 `حبالهم`, `عصيهم`; 26:45 `فألقى`
- Synthesis: The scene assembles simple implements whose ordinary functions are redirected into spectacle. Rope can bind or snare, staff can support, and casting places both under a fabricated motion. Their material ordinariness heightens the contest over what the eye is being made to see.

#### Subchannel B. Serpent, Opening, and Swallowing
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A staff becomes a great serpent whose rapid swallowing overturns the manufactured display.
- Active motifs: great serpent (`quranic:root_000199:B002/m01`); opening or channeling water (`quranic:root_000199:B001/m01`); rapid swallowing (`quranic:root_001370:B001/m01`); overturning a thing (`quranic:root_000041:B001/m01`); fabricated falsehood (`quranic:root_000041:B002/m01`); reversal of orientation (`quranic:root_001248:B004/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:32 `ثعبان`; 26:45 `تلقف`, `يافكون`; 26:46 `فالقى`; 26:50 `منقلبون`
- Synthesis: The serpent does more than appear: it ingests what the rivals produce. The same root's water-opening sense gives its extension a channel-like motion, while overturning and swallowing specify the present operation: fabricated appearance is taken inside and removed.

### 7. Rank and Allegiance Reversed (P2, 26:21-51)
- Semantic invariant: A hierarchy organized by wages, victory, and royal proximity is abruptly replaced by prostration, belief, return, and hoped-for forgiveness.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:40-42 negotiates reward and proximity, 26:46-48 enacts prostration and faith, and 26:49-51 rejects royal harm in favor of return to God.
- Surprising reach: Bodily lowering produces moral elevation, while threatened loss becomes the route by which the contestants name their true destination.

#### Subchannel A. Contracted Victory and Proximity
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Skilled agents bargain for compensation and elevated access if their performance secures domination.
- Active motifs: stipulated wage (`quranic:root_000015:B001/m01`); prevailing force (`quranic:root_001098:B001/m01`); royal proximity (`quranic:root_001212:B004/m01`); elevated rank (`quranic:root_001281:B005/m01`); conquest or overcoming (`quranic:root_001008:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:40 `الغلبين`; 26:41 `لاجرا`, `الغلبين`; 26:42 `المقربين`; 26:44 `بعزة`; 26:49 `لكبيركم`
- Synthesis: Wage and proximity disclose the social contract beneath the contest. Victory is a purchasable service, and rank is its promised payment. This prepares the reversal in which the performers abandon both compensation and patron.

#### Subchannel B. Prostration as Reclassification
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: The defeated performers are cast into prostration and identify themselves as believers under a different Lord.
- Active motifs: bodily prostration (`quranic:root_000675:B001/m01`); submissive orientation (`quranic:root_000675:B004/m01`); believing trust (`quranic:root_000054:B002/m01`); transformed status (`quranic:root_000248:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:29 `لاجعلنك`; 26:46 `سجدين`; 26:47 `ءامنا`; 26:47-48 `رب`
- Synthesis: Being `ألقي` into prostration reverses the agency of their earlier casting. The posture is not merely defeat; it reclassifies affiliation and rank, replacing the royal ladder of proximity with submission to the Lord of Moses and Aaron.

#### Subchannel C. Return Beyond Harm
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Threatened subjects declare injury inconsequential, orient toward return, and seek forgiveness for prior fault.
- Active motifs: injury or constraining harm (`quranic:root_000921:B001/m01`); reversal and return (`quranic:root_001248:B005/m01`); expectant hope (`quranic:root_000951:B001/m01`); covering forgiveness (`quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`); moral fault (`quranic:root_000420:B002/m01`); final destination (`quranic:root_000067:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:50 `لا ضير`, `منقلبون`; 26:51 `نطمع`, `يغفر`, `خطينا`, `اول`
- Synthesis: The declaration `لا ضير` does not deny bodily pain; it denies Pharaoh the power to define its final consequence. Return and forgiveness relocate outcome beyond royal punishment, turning threatened bodily reversal into an eschatological reorientation.

### 8. Cosmic Bounds and Discernment (P2, 26:21-51)
- Semantic invariant: True lordship is recognized through ordered spatial limits and the faculties capable of receiving their evidence.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:23-28 expands lordship through heavens, earth, the interval, east, west, hearing, certainty, and reason.
- Surprising reach: Spatial orientation and cognitive orientation mirror one another: bounded directions become a test of whether an audience can itself turn, hear, and infer.

#### Subchannel A. Encompassed Space and Horizons
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Heavens and lower earth establish vertical bounds, the interval relates them, and sunrise and sunset establish the opposed horizontal horizons.
- Active motifs: upper sky (`quranic:root_000745:B004/m01`); lower earth (`quranic:root_000025:B001/m01`); separating interval (`quranic:root_000170:B002/m01`); relation between two sides (`quranic:root_000170:B003/m01`); sunrise and east (`quranic:root_000790:B001/m01`); sunset and west (`quranic:root_001077:B006/m01`); remoteness of a horizon (`quranic:root_001077:B007/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:24 `السموت`, `الارض`, `بينهما`; 26:28 `المشرق`, `المغرب`, `بينهما`
- Synthesis: The answer to "what is the Lord" is staged as an ordered field rather than a definition. Vertical and horizontal limits, together with what lies between, make sovereignty legible through encompassing relation and recurrent orientation.

#### Subchannel B. Hearing, Reason, and Certainty
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Addressed listeners move from acoustic reception toward comprehension, inferential restraint, knowledge, and settled certainty.
- Active motifs: hearing sound (`quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`); hearing that entails response (`quranic:root_000741:B003/m01`); restraining reason (`quranic:root_001036:B001/m01`); restraint of the tongue (`quranic:root_001036:B003/m01`); acquired knowledge (`quranic:root_001040:B001/m01`); evidentiary marker (`quranic:root_001040:B002/m01`); settled certainty (`quranic:root_001696:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:24 `موقنين`; 26:25 `تستمعون`; 26:28 `تعقلون`; 26:34, 26:37-38 `عليم`, `معلوم`
- Synthesis: Pharaoh's appeals to the court expose a gap between sound and responsive hearing. Moses' sequence asks for certainty and reason, while the latent restraint senses suggest that cognition requires checking impulse and speech rather than merely possessing information.

### 9. Freedom and Claimed Benefaction (P2, 26:21-51)
- Semantic invariant: Competing accounts assign opposite meanings to escape, patronage, judgment, and the release or enslavement of people.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:21 names flight, fear, gifted judgment, and commission, while 26:22 contests Pharaoh's presentation of Israelite enslavement as a favor.
- Surprising reach: A benefaction claim is exposed as moral debt-making: nurture and patronage become instruments for claiming ownership over the released person.

#### Subchannel A. Flight Reframed as Commission
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A fearful fugitive escapes one jurisdiction, receives a gift of judgment, and returns with transformed standing as a messenger.
- Active motifs: flight and escape (`quranic:root_001142:B001/m01`); fear before threat (`quranic:root_000447:B001/m01`); unearned gift (`quranic:root_001685:B001/m01`); preparation by gifting (`quranic:root_001685:B005/m01`); adjudicating judgment (`quranic:root_000348:B002/m01`); practical wisdom (`quranic:root_000348:B003/m01`); transformed rank (`quranic:root_000248:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:21 `ففررت`, `خفتكم`, `فوهب`, `حكما`, `وجعلنى`, `المرسلين`
- Synthesis: Flight initially marks exposure and loss of standing. Gifted judgment converts that movement into preparation, and commission supplies a new rank not granted by the court from which Moses fled.

#### Subchannel B. Enslavement Disguised as Favor
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A patron recalls a benefit in order to impose gratitude, while the alleged beneficiary points to the mass subjection that made the benefit possible.
- Active motifs: servile bondage (`quranic:root_000973:B001/m01`); active enslavement (`quranic:root_000973:B004/m01`); bestowed favor (`quranic:root_001525:B001/m01`); burdening another with recalled favor (`quranic:root_001449:B003/m01`); freeing a captive without price (`quranic:root_001449:B004/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:22 `نعمة`, `تمنها`, `عبدت`, `بنى`
- Synthesis: The exchange distinguishes a gift from the rhetoric of gift. `تمنها` carries the pressure of repeatedly naming a favor, while enslavement reveals the unpaid social cost beneath it. The latent release sense sharpens the missing act: genuine benefaction would free rather than claim.

### 10. Pursuit to Convergence (P3, 26:52-68)
- Semantic invariant: Separated groups are set into directed motion until traces, timing, and sight bring them into one field of encounter.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:52 orders covert night travel, 26:53-60 mobilizes pursuit, and 26:61 makes the two gatherings mutually visible.
- Surprising reach: Communication, tracking, and collective motion form a single detection process in which secrecy is progressively stripped away.

#### Subchannel A. Covert Departure and Tracked Following
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A hidden night departure is disclosed through traces, prompting a cautious state apparatus to accelerate in pursuit.
- Active motifs: travel by night (`quranic:root_000702:B001/m01`); uncovering what is hidden (`quranic:root_000702:B004/m01`); secret communication (`quranic:root_001633:B001/m01`); accelerated movement (`quranic:root_001633:B006/m01`); servile subjects (`quranic:root_000973:B001/m01`); following a trail (`quranic:root_000175:B001/m01`); catching up from behind (`quranic:root_000175:B002/m01`); material trace (`quranic:root_000175:B003/m01`); guarded readiness (`quranic:root_000301:B003/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:52 `اسر`, `بعبادى`, `متبعون`; 26:56 `حذرون`; 26:60 `فاتبعوهم`
- Synthesis: Night travel creates temporary concealment, but following converts prior movement into readable trace. The regime's caution and speed show pursuit as an information process as much as a military one: the departed body's route becomes evidence for the pursuer.

#### Subchannel B. Gathering into Mutual Sight
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Dispersed forces are driven together, one side classifies the other as a small detached band, and both collectives enter visual range before anticipated capture.
- Active motifs: directing a crowd to one goal (`quranic:root_000324:B001/m01`); gathering dispersed members (`quranic:root_000259:B001/m01`); formed collective (`quranic:root_000259:B002/m01`); small detached group (`quranic:root_000786:B001/m01`); cut-off fragment (`quranic:root_000786:B002/m01`); reciprocal seeing (`quranic:root_000531:B004/m01`); overtaking and capture (`quranic:root_000471:B001/m01`); companions under one fate (`quranic:root_000844:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:53 `حشرين`; 26:54 `لشرذمة`; 26:56 `جميع`; 26:61 `ترءا`, `الجمعان`, `اصحب`, `لمدركون`
- Synthesis: Muster and pursuit culminate in reciprocal visibility. The two gatherings are no longer abstract populations but opposed formations sharing one visual field, and the companions correctly read the surface geometry as imminent capture before guidance changes that geometry.

### 11. Sea as Partitioned Passage (P3, 26:52-68)
- Semantic invariant: An apparent barrier is struck, divided, and stabilized into a route that saves one collective and closes over another.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:63-66 names striking, splitting, mountain-like parts, approach, rescue, and drowning.
- Surprising reach: The same material becomes wall, road, and grave solely through sequence and allocated passage.

#### Subchannel A. Struck Water, Cleft Walls, Open Route
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A staff strikes a mass of water, opens a cleft, and holds the separated portions like great walls around a traversable interval.
- Active motifs: broad abundant water (`quranic:root_000086:B001/m01`); wide cleft (`quranic:root_000086:B003/m01`); basin holding water (`quranic:root_000086:B006/m01`); impact of one thing on another (`quranic:root_000906:B001/m01`); staff as tool (`quranic:root_005713:B001/m01`); staff applied in striking (`quranic:root_005713:B005/m01`); cleaving apart (`quranic:root_001176:B001/m01`); open fissure (`quranic:root_001176:B004/m01`); distinction between parts (`quranic:root_001148:B001/m01`); split-off portion (`quranic:root_001148:B004/m01`); great mountain mass (`quranic:root_000954:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:63 `اضرب`, `بعصاك`, `البحر`, `فانفلق`, `فرق`, `كالطود`, `العظيم`
- Synthesis: The event is a temporary engineering of matter. Impact and cleaving separate the sea; mountain-like stability prevents immediate collapse; the interval becomes a way. The scene is tight because every motif participates in producing or maintaining one passage.

#### Subchannel B. Extraction and Closure
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: One group is brought through intact, the pursuers are drawn into the same opening, and closure converts approach into engulfment.
- Active motifs: drawing the other side near (`quranic:root_000639:B001/m01`); rescue by separation (`quranic:root_001476:B001/m01`); complete extraction (`quranic:root_001476:B003/m01`); elevated safe ground (`quranic:root_001476:B004/m01`); submersion (`quranic:root_001080:B001/m01`); annihilating flood (`quranic:root_001080:B005/m01`); latter or other side (`quranic:root_000019:B001/m01`); complete gathered group (`quranic:root_000259:B009/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:64 `ازلفنا`; 26:65 `انجينا`, `ومن معه`, `اجمعين`; 26:66 `اغرقنا`, `الءاخرين`
- Synthesis: Rescue and drowning are not separate water images but opposed outcomes of one controlled opening. Extraction preserves a whole collective; approach admits the other; surrounding water then makes the latter the remainder enclosed within the route.

### 12. Inert Gods and Failed Support (P4, 26:69-104)
- Semantic invariant: Objects and relationships treated as sources of aid are tested for perception, agency, and effective support, then shown unable to act.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:70-77 interrogates worship, hearing, benefit, and harm, while 26:92-101 exposes absent gods, intercessors, and close friends.
- Surprising reach: The critique moves from inert material objects to equally inert social capital, testing divine and human supports by the same operational criterion.

#### Subchannel A. Devotion to Inert Objects
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A community remains attached to fashioned objects that receive repeated service but cannot hear, answer, benefit, or injure.
- Active motifs: fashioned idol (`quranic:root_000886:B001/m01`); ritual servitude (`quranic:root_000973:B003/m01`); fixed devotion (`quranic:root_001038:B001/m01`); clinging attendance (`quranic:root_001038:B004/m01`); called addressee (`quranic:root_000478:B001/m01`); acoustic hearing (`quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`); benefit supplied (`quranic:root_001536:B001/m01`); inflicted harm (`quranic:root_000907:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:70 `تعبدون`; 26:71 `اصناما`, `عكفين`; 26:72 `يسمعون`, `تدعون`; 26:73 `ينفعونكم`, `يضرون`
- Synthesis: The worship scene is evaluated as a failed exchange. Attention and service flow toward the objects, but no perception or effect returns. Persistent attendance therefore materializes the asymmetry rather than proving the objects' efficacy.

#### Subchannel B. Inherited Field Redrawn as Enmity
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The worshipper reassesses what his people found in ancient practice and places every former object of service on the hostile side except the sovereign Lord.
- Active motifs: crossing a proper limit (`quranic:root_000993:B001/m01`); hostile enemy (`quranic:root_000993:B003/m01`); being unlike or other (`quranic:root_000766:B007/m01`); sovereign nurturer (`quranic:root_000532:B001/m01`); finding what is present (`quranic:root_001626:B001/m01`); established existence (`quranic:root_001626:B002/m01`); ancient prior time (`quranic:root_001207:B003/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:74 `وجدنا`, `ءاباءنا`; 26:75 `تعبدون`; 26:76 `انتم`, `ءاباؤكم`, `الاقدمون`; 26:77 `عدو`, `الا`, `رب`; 26:98 `نسويكم`
- Synthesis: What the community found established in ancient practice is not merely downgraded; it is transferred into an opposing class. The explicit exception isolates the sovereign Lord from the inherited field, while enmity names the new operational relation to its former objects.

#### Subchannel C. Absent Mediation and Kin
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: At exposure, expected mediators and intimate allies fail to interpose, leaving the subject without effective relational support.
- Active motifs: joining one thing to its like (`quranic:root_000802:B001/m01`); mediator who joins another side (`quranic:root_000802:B002/m01`); intimate warmth (`quranic:root_000001:B011/m01`); close companion (`quranic:root_000852:B005/m01`); help or victory (`quranic:root_001510:B001/m01`); redress for the wronged (`quranic:root_001510:B002/m01`); effective benefit (`quranic:root_001536:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:73 `ينفعونكم`; 26:88 `ينفع`; 26:93 `ينصرونكم`; 26:100 `شفعين`; 26:101 `صديق`, `حميم`
- Synthesis: Intercession and intimate friendship are distinct social mechanisms: one negotiates across sides, the other supplies closeness and loyalty. Their joint absence extends the failed-support test from idols to human networks, neither of which can produce benefit at the decisive moment.

### 13. Care Across the Life Cycle (P4, 26:69-104)
- Semantic invariant: Sustaining lordship is recognized through coordinated acts that originate, orient, nourish, repair, end, restore, and forgive a life.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:78-82 presents creation, guidance, food, drink, illness, healing, death, life, and hoped-for forgiveness as a continuous first-person sequence.
- Surprising reach: Care is not reduced to protection from breakdown; illness, death, and moral fault are integrated into a cycle whose decisive operations remain restoration and renewed life.

#### Subchannel A. Origination and Guidance
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A formed creature is brought into determinate shape and then directed along a viable course.
- Active motifs: creating from an initial measure (`quranic:root_000434:B001/m01`); forming a creature (`quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`); bringing a process to completion (`quranic:root_000434:B003/m01`); route guidance (`quranic:root_001583:B001/m01`); guidance toward a destination (`quranic:root_001583:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:78 `خلقنى`, `يهدين`
- Synthesis: Creation and guidance are sequential rather than interchangeable. Formation supplies a capable being; direction carries that being through a world in which mere origination would not ensure arrival.

#### Subchannel B. Feeding and Watering
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Hunger and thirst are met by recurring provision that enters and sustains the body.
- Active motifs: tasting and taking food (`quranic:root_000934:B001/m01`); feeding another (`quranic:root_000934:B002/m01`); livelihood and provision (`quranic:root_000934:B004/m01`); giving drink (`quranic:root_000722:B001/m01`); assigned water share or channel (`quranic:root_000722:B003/m01`); heavy raincloud (`quranic:root_000722:B007/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:79 `يطعمنى`, `يسقين`
- Synthesis: Feeding and watering form a paired maintenance operation that moves provision into the body. The water-share and raincloud senses extend bodily sustenance into allocated and atmospheric supply, reinforcing care as a recurrent system rather than a single rescue.

#### Subchannel C. Illness and Healing
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Bodily disorder is acknowledged without being attributed as care, while healing is assigned as the restoring operation.
- Active motifs: bodily illness (`quranic:root_001415:B001/m01`); tending the sick (`quranic:root_001415:B003/m01`); weakened movement (`quranic:root_001415:B004/m01`); healing and cure (`quranic:root_000806:B001/m01`); edge or brink (`quranic:root_000806:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:80 `مرضت`, `يشفين`
- Synthesis: The grammar separates the onset of disorder from the agency of cure. Weak movement and sick-tending give illness a bodily and relational structure, while the same healing root's brink sense usefully figures cure as removal from an exposed edge.

#### Subchannel D. Death, Revival, and Forgiveness
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Life is ended and renewed, while moral fault is covered in hope of a favorable outcome at judgment.
- Active motifs: departure of force and life (`quranic:root_001454:B001/m01`); causing death (`quranic:root_001454:B002/m01`); stillness and extinction (`quranic:root_001454:B012/m01`); earth revived by rain and growth (`quranic:root_000383:B002/m01`); animate living creature (`quranic:root_000383:B003/m01`); sparing and preserving life (`quranic:root_000383:B006/m01`); life as benefit and good (`quranic:root_000383:B013/m01`); covering forgiveness (`quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:81 `يميتنى`, `يحيين`; 26:82 `يغفر`, `خطيتي`, `الدين`
- Synthesis: Death and revival complete the bodily cycle, but forgiveness adds a moral restoration that is not reducible to biological return. The sequence makes life-cycle care include the repaired standing of the person as well as renewed vitality.

### 14. Moral Inheritance and Durable Worth (P4, 26:69-104)
- Semantic invariant: What endures is an inward and transmitted moral condition, not inherited lineage, accumulated assets, or temporary social backing.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:83-89 asks for judgment, righteous company, truthful later remembrance, inheritance, forgiveness, and a sound heart, while 26:100-101 removes intercessors and intimate allies.
- Surprising reach: Inheritance moves from estate and descendants to judgment, truthful speech, and interior soundness, redefining what can actually cross generations and judgment.

#### Subchannel A. Gifted Judgment and Righteous Company
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A gift of practical judgment joins its recipient to a community characterized by repaired and fitting action.
- Active motifs: unearned gift (`quranic:root_001685:B001/m01`); adjudicating judgment (`quranic:root_000348:B002/m01`); practical wisdom (`quranic:root_000348:B003/m01`); repaired righteousness (`quranic:root_000876:B001/m01`); fitness for a relation (`quranic:root_000876:B003/m01`); relational joining (`quranic:root_001347:B001/m01`); incorporation into a class (`quranic:root_001347:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:83 `هب`, `حكما`, `الحقنى`, `بالصلحين`
- Synthesis: Judgment is requested not as solitary status but as the capacity to belong within righteous practice. Gift, repair, fitness, and joining form a social-moral scene in which wisdom is validated by the company and conduct it enables.

#### Subchannel B. Truthful Tongue Across Generations
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Truthful speech becomes a durable name carried by later communities after the speaker's own lifetime.
- Active motifs: tongue as bearer (`quranic:root_001355:B001/m01`); eloquent expression (`quranic:root_001355:B003/m01`); shared language (`quranic:root_001355:B006/m01`); truthful correspondence (`quranic:root_000852:B001/m01`); confirmed truthfulness (`quranic:root_000852:B004/m01`); trusted companion (`quranic:root_000852:B005/m01`); later posterity (`quranic:root_000019:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:84 `لسان`, `صدق`, `الءاخرين`
- Synthesis: The requested `لسان صدق` binds organ, speech, reputation, and later reception. Its durability is relational: later speakers preserve a truthful name because utterance and life correspond, not because descent alone carries it.

#### Subchannel C. Inheritance Reassigned
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Estate, garden, blessing, and filial succession are gathered into the language of inheritance, then redirected toward a moral and eschatological possession.
- Active motifs: inherited transfer (`quranic:root_001639:B001/m01`); inherited knowledge or virtue (`quranic:root_001639:B003/m01`); cultivated garden (`quranic:root_000266:B003/m01`); bestowed blessing (`quranic:root_001525:B001/m01`); paternal relation (`quranic:root_000007:B001/m01`); filial lineage (`quranic:root_000156:B007/m01`); accumulated wealth (`quranic:root_001457:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:85 `ورثة`, `جنة`; 26:86 `لابى`; 26:88 `مال`, `بنون`
- Synthesis: The request for inheritance stands beside concern for a father and the later failure of wealth and sons. This arrangement pressures ordinary succession: what is sought is not simply an estate transferred through lineage, but durable participation in a garden that external capital cannot buy.

#### Subchannel D. Sound Core Beyond External Capital
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: At judgment, the person's interior center is tested while wealth, descendants, friends, and mediators lose their purchasing and protective force.
- Active motifs: inner heart (`quranic:root_001248:B001/m01`); cognitive-moral core (`quranic:root_001248:B002/m01`); sound integrity (`quranic:root_000737:B001/m01`); arriving before another (`quranic:root_000009:B001/m01`); accumulated wealth (`quranic:root_001457:B001/m01`); filial descendants (`quranic:root_000156:B007/m01`); effective benefit (`quranic:root_001536:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:88 `مال`, `بنون`, `ينفع`; 26:89 `اتى`, `بقلب`, `سليم`
- Synthesis: Arrival with a sound heart reverses the expected logic of capital. The only transferable condition is inward integrity; possessions and descendants remain external and therefore cannot perform the needed operation of benefit.

### 15. Exposed Judgment and Collapsing Assembly (P4, 26:69-104)
- Semantic invariant: Judgment makes hidden destinations visible, drives false collectives into a common enclosure, and turns retrospective dispute into recognition without escape.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:87-102 moves through resurrection, exposed garden and hell, collective casting, dispute, failed support, and an impossible wish to return.
- Surprising reach: Communities assembled by shared error remain assembled in ruin, while the once-hidden objects of hope become visually near yet operationally unreachable.

#### Subchannel A. Destinations Brought into View
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Resurrection exposes and draws near opposed destinations so that bliss and punishment become visible conditions.
- Active motifs: movement into nearness (`quranic:root_000639:B001/m01`); close rank or proximity (`quranic:root_000639:B002/m01`); visible exposure (`quranic:root_000105:B001/m01`); open exposed ground (`quranic:root_000105:B002/m01`); blazing fire (`quranic:root_000225:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:87 `يبعثون`; 26:90 `ازلفت`, `الجنة`; 26:91 `برزت`, `الجحيم`
- Synthesis: Nearness and exposure convert promised outcomes into an immediate visual field. Garden and fire are not merely announced; they are brought forward, stripping away the distance that had enabled denial.

#### Subchannel B. Heap, Army, and Pit
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Errant agents and their supporters are overturned together, piled into an enclosure, and deprived of the collective force they once represented.
- Active motifs: piled headlong casting (`quranic:root_001282:B001/m01`); error opposed to right guidance (`quranic:root_001116:B001/m01`); hunter's fatal pit (`quranic:root_001116:B004/m01`); mutually reinforcing host (`quranic:root_000264:B001/m01`); complete gathered mass (`quranic:root_000259:B009/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:94 `فكبكبوا`, `الغاون`; 26:95 `جنود`, `اجمعون`
- Synthesis: Repetition in `كبكبوا` supplies tumbling accumulation rather than orderly entry. The army's former coordination survives only as a mass: collective strength is inverted into collective confinement.

#### Subchannel C. Dispute Without Return
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Members of the collapsed assembly argue over misclassification, acknowledge misleading agents, and imagine a reversal that can no longer be enacted.
- Active motifs: adversarial dispute (`quranic:root_000416:B001/m01`); manifest error (`quranic:root_000913:B001/m01`); admitted crime (`quranic:root_000239:B004/m01`); repeated return (`quranic:root_001292:B001/m01`); reversal and outcome (`quranic:root_001248:B005/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:89 `بقلب`; 26:96 `يختصمون`; 26:97 `ضلل`; 26:99 `اضلنا`; 26:102 `كرة`, `المؤمنين`
- Synthesis: Dispute identifies error and criminal responsibility only after their consequences are fixed. The desired `كرة` is a repeated return and reversal of outcome, but it remains speech rather than movement; recognition arrives after the route back has closed.

### 16. Messenger Trust Outside Wages (P5, 26:105-122)
- Semantic invariant: Legitimate warning rests on entrusted transmission and accountable conduct rather than purchased loyalty or social rank.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:105-110 joins denial, brotherly address, trustworthiness, reverence, obedience, and refusal of wages.
- Surprising reach: The no-fee formula is not merely economic disclaiming; it removes the messenger from the patronage economy that structures competing authority.

#### Subchannel A. Entrusted Commission
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A messenger stands among kin as a trusted bearer whose proper response is protective restraint and obedience.
- Active motifs: messenger and message (`quranic:root_000563:B002/m01`); entrusted faithfulness (`quranic:root_000054:B001/m01`); awakening warning (`quranic:root_001488:B001/m01`); protective restraint (`quranic:root_001677:B001/m01`); obedient compliance (`quranic:root_000956:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:106 `اخوهم`, `تتقون`; 26:107 `رسول`, `امين`; 26:108 `فاتقوا`, `واطيعون`; 26:115 `نذير`
- Synthesis: Kinship supplies proximity but not authority. The commission is grounded in trustworthy carriage of a message, and obedience is framed as restraint against a breach rather than submission to inherited status.

#### Subchannel B. Unpurchased Labor and Account
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The messenger performs communicative labor without taking a local fee because recompense and final accounting belong to another sovereign.
- Active motifs: asking or requesting (`quranic:root_000661:B001/m01`); wage for labor (`quranic:root_000015:B001/m01`); sovereign provision (`quranic:root_000532:B001/m01`); intended work (`quranic:root_001046:B001/m01`); worker's wage and livelihood (`quranic:root_001046:B004/m01`); reckoning (`quranic:root_000318:B001/m01`); sufficiency that makes independent (`quranic:root_000318:B003/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:109 `اسلكم`, `اجر`, `اجرى`, `رب`; 26:112 `عمل`; 26:113 `حسابهم`
- Synthesis: Refusing wages separates warning from transaction. Work remains real and countable, but its compensation and audit are displaced from the audience to the Lord, preventing hearers from converting payment into control over the message.

### 17. Social Sorting and Vessel Inclusion (P5, 26:105-122)
- Semantic invariant: Competing authorities attempt to draw the boundary of the legitimate community, while rescue ultimately materializes belonging as inclusion within a filled vessel.
- Surface relation: direct; 26:111-116 contests low-status followers and expulsion, while 26:119 gathers Noah and his companions into the laden ark.
- Surprising reach: A social argument over whom to cast out is answered by a physical container whose protected capacity includes the very community being despised.

#### Subchannel A. Low Followers and Refusal to Expel
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Elite challengers classify followers as socially low, but the messenger refuses to drive away people whose work is not his to judge.
- Active motifs: following another's path (`quranic:root_000175:B001/m01`); attached follower (`quranic:root_000175:B004/m01`); socially abject position (`quranic:root_000559:B001/m01`); expelling from a place (`quranic:root_000930:B001/m01`); continuous driving away (`quranic:root_000930:B004/m01`); believing affiliation (`quranic:root_000054:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 26:111 `اتبعك`, `الارذلون`; 26:114 `بطارد`, `المؤمنين`
